objective: Assess Codex auto-review as a security control: whether a model or repository content can bypass, disable or mislead it, and whether it leaks data.
scope: Commit 08b054b on release/0.3.1/feat/auto-review in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-autoreview (range 91d9eb07..08b054b); source diff without generated dist at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad/auto-review-commit.diff; writer report /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw9wh8o1-xebk.md; design research /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw96z5n3-mw6f.md.
Testing rule: unit tests with recorded or synthesized fixtures only; the reviewer request is made through an injectable client so tests never reach a network.
Testing rule: never start pi or make a model or network request; unit tests only.

Points to trace: classifier bypasses (shell quoting, command substitution, aliases, env tricks, path tricks to write outside the root, symlinks, tools that write through other names such as apply_patch, edit, write and MCP tools); fail-open paths (exceptions, schema decode, timeouts, the breaker, the /approve override and whether a model or tool output can trigger it); prompt injection from the untrusted transcript into the reviewer; config keys that replace the policy and whether a repository-level config can weaken it; what the request sends off-machine.
constraints: Make no edits and no git writes.
Report in under 400 words; put long logs in a file in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad and give its path.

result:
result: blockers found. The classifier, the config path and the path-containment check all have validated bypasses. Nothing was executed; every finding below is from reading code, because this session has no shell.

The built-in `/security-review` could not run. It failed on `git diff origin/HEAD...` with "unknown revision", since `origin/HEAD` is not set. I reviewed `91d9eb07..08b054b` by hand from the worktree source.

changed: none

blockers:
1. **Brace expansion defeats the safe-command flag checks.**
   - Source: model-chosen `bash` command. Sink: shell execution, unreviewed.
   - `splitCommand` in `classify.ts` blocks `$`, backtick, `\`, `<>()#!` but not `{}`. The `UNSAFE_*` checks compare the unexpanded word, so `rg --p{re,re}=./x.sh foo .` passes `safeProgram`. Bash expands it to `--pre=./x.sh` and ripgrep runs the script on every file.
   - `x.sh` is created beforehand with the `write` tool inside the root, which is also unreviewed.
   - `git log --out{put,put}=/home/u/.bashrc` passes `UNSAFE_GIT` the same way and overwrites a file outside the root.
2. **Safe set contains runners and writers.**
   - `git grep -O"sh ./x.sh" foo`: `-O` (`--open-files-in-pager`) runs a command, and `UNSAFE_GIT` has no `-O`.
   - `uniq in /outside/path` writes its second argument; `uniq` is in `SAFE_PROGRAMS`.
   - Codex's sandbox contained these. Pi has no sandbox, so the classifier is the only control.
3. **The model or the repository can switch auto-review off.**
   - The project `.holyagent/config.json` wins the merge; `FINAL_OFF` in `config/load.ts` locks only computerUse, web and deviceAccess.
   - A repository that ships `pi.features.autoReview:false`, `pi.provider` set to another provider, `pi.enable:false`, or a replacement `pi.autoReview.policy` of "allow everything" runs with no effective review.
   - A malformed project config also disables it. `read` stays unset, so `closedSettings` uses the default config and `codex` is `undefined`, while the session model is still Codex.
   - The model can do it mid-session. `write .holyagent/config.json` is "inside root" and unreviewed. `session_compact` then re-runs `gather` and replaces `held.codex`.
4. **Path containment is lexical and differs from Pi.**
   - Pi's `write` and `edit` strip a leading `@`, expand `~/` and convert `file://` URLs. `isOutsideRoot` does none of this.
   - `@/etc/x`, `@~/.ssh/authorized_keys` and `file:///etc/x` all look inside the root and are not reviewed.
   - A symlink committed in the repository (`link -> ~/.ssh`) makes `write link/authorized_keys` unreviewed. The docs admit links are not resolved.
   - `.git/config` (`core.fsmonitor`, then a "safe" `git status` runs it) and `.git/hooks` are in-root and unreviewed.
5. **Plausible, unconfirmed: other tools are not classified.** Any tool that is not `bash`, `write`, `edit`, `apply_patch` or a web tool, and has no MCP annotations, runs unreviewed. The pinned `@aliou/pi-processes` and `codemode` packages are not installed here, so I could not confirm they take a `command` or run inner tool calls without a `tool_call` event.

notes:
- Suspicion, not validated: the transcript has no escaping. A tool result can forge `>>> TRANSCRIPT END`, `[n] user:` lines or a `developer:` line carrying `MANUAL_APPROVAL_PREFIX`. Assistant text is included, so the model can also claim authorization.
- Sound:
  - Reviewer failures, a bad decode and a thrown handler all block. Pi's `emitToolCall` also blocks on a throw.
  - A timeout never allows.
  - `/approve` is a user command only, and it covers one exact action.
  - The request uses `redirect:"error"` and `store:false`, and the token goes only in headers.
  - What leaves the machine is the transcript, which can include file contents, and it goes to the same Codex backend as the main model.
  - `apply_patch` rejects paths outside the working directory (`apply-patch.ts:399`).

evidence:
findings: items 1 to 5 above, with `classify.ts` lines 157-198 (splitter), 96-126 (unsafe lists), 220-224 (`isOutsideRoot`), `config/load.ts:50-54` (`FINAL_OFF`), `extension.ts:1052-1066`, 1418 and 1474-1475 (`closedSettings` and `gather`), and Pi `utils/paths.js:100-123`.
